title: Investigate and patch Hosted timeouts from TLS session reuse + Dedicated warmup; customer bridge + replay tooling
creator: Marcus Nguyen
description: Customer-reported escalations (two enterprise customers) show sudden spikes in 502/504 timeouts for hosted inference endpoints coinciding with scheduled Dedicated pool reshuffles. Symptoms: long tail request latency, connection stalls in frontdoor edge, and downstream runtime timeouts. Initial triage indicates a collision between TLS session reuse semantics at the edge/proxy layer and the Dedicated warmup/eviction sequence that causes a class of requests to block waiting for a re-established KV cache and blocked connection handoff. Retries from client SDKs amplify the effect, causing tenant-visible 5xx waves. This ticket tracks investigation, runtime/edge patch, temporary customer-bridge mitigations, and creation of an isolated 'replay' harness that reproduces the burst pattern against a Dedicated-like environment for postmortem verification.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use synthetic tenant traffic generator to fire 500 concurrent short requests with keepalive reuse enabled
2) Trigger Dedicated pool reshard/eviction event to simulate warmup (scale-down then scale-up of worker nodes),
3) Observe edge logs for TLS session renegotiation delays and 502/504 spikes in /api/v1/generate,
4) Replay same load but with SDK retry disabled to show lower amplification and fewer 5xxs
root_cause_summary: Race between edge TLS session reuse and Dedicated worker lifecycle: edge attempted to reuse a TCP/TLS session that the Dedicated backend had already torn down during a reshard, causing connections to hang in I/O wait inside the proxy. The runtime attempted to reconstruct KV cache synchronously for these re-established connections, which serialized token generation and triggered host-side timeouts. Client SDK retries without proper idempotency tokens caused request amplification and cascade across tenants.
proposed_fix: Edge/proxy: treat TLS session reuse mismatch as fast-failable; return a short-lived 409-style handshake-failed header to prompt immediate client reconnect rather than blocking
Runtime: make KV cache rehydration asynchronous during connection rebind; allow inflight request fastpath to fallback to in-memory prefix cache where safe
Admission controller: add per-tenant inflight cap with jittered backoff that emits telemetry to Hosted Console
SDK: publish patch to default exponential-retry to include an idempotency token generation window; temporarily reduce retry attempts for generate endpoints
Dedicated orchestrator: emit a soft-drain signal before eviction and delay hard teardown until proxy acknowledges connection handoff
temporary_mitigation: Enable customer-specific route fallback to a compatible hosted model variant with isolated capacity for affected tenants (customer-bridge),
Apply edge proxy config change to lower keepalive reuse window for affected regions from 300s to 30s for the next 48 hours
Advise customers to upgrade SDK to 1.4.2-hotfix which disables aggressive retries for generation calls
Manual scaled-up standby pool for affected Dedicated customers until patch rollout completes
rollout_plan: Canary: deploy edge fast-fail change to 1% of traffic in us-west-2 for 1 hour; monitor 5xx rate and tail latency
Incremental: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 24 hours if 5xx delta < 0.05% and P95 latency improves
Runtime: deploy async-KV rehydration in the runtime with feature flag; enable for internal canary tenants first
SDK: publish patch and coordinate customer outreach for immediate upgrade; include opt-in instructions for SDK rollback
Rollback: automatic rollback if 5xxs increase by >0.5% sustained for 10 minutes or if error budget breach triggers
